entries.title: Skycompass
entries.summary: A converted craftable navigation instrument that indicates celestial time and approximate direction when ordinary visibility fails.
body: A skycompass is a polished crystal held in a brass frame. Moving points of light within the crystal align to the Material Plane’s sun, moon, and stars even through clouds, underground, or under ordinary magical concealment.

The instrument is valuable because it provides orientation rather than a complete route. It cannot identify a destination, distinguish planes, compensate for a false chart, or replace a trained navigator.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 rules
body: Price 750 gp; weight 1 lb.; faint divination; caster level 3rd; construction requires Craft (precision instruments) or Craft (mechanical) 5 ranks and either Knowledge (geography) 5 ranks or access to a divination caster.
While held and studied for 1 minute, the skycompass reveals approximate cardinal direction and local time of day or night on the Material Plane.
It grants a +2 competence bonus on Survival and Profession (navigator) checks made to maintain direction or determine position from celestial references.
It does not function across planar boundaries and cannot determine altitude, exact coordinates, or whether the surrounding chart is accurate.

sections.heading: Crafting profile
body: Complexity: Complex; project DC 20; 6 work units; raw materials 250 gp.
Required components: precision brass frame, calibrated crystal, celestial reference chart, silver wire, and a stable observation point for final calibration.

Research skill: Knowledge (geography), Knowledge (the planes), or Spellcraft. Construction skill: Craft (precision instruments) or Craft (mechanical). Testing skill: Profession (navigator) or Survival.
Common flaw: the device is accurate only by day or only by night, or develops a 45-degree directional error after exposure to strong magic until recalibrated.

sourceRefs.notes: Converted equipment rules and crafting profile.

entries.title: Tattered Trade Route Map
entries.summary: A converted enchanted regional chart that preserves route memory, assists navigation, and can reveal overlooked camps or caches.
body: This weathered chart records a once-important route through landmarks, favored inns, shortcuts, marginal warnings, and the remembered habits of previous travelers.
Its enchantment adjusts minor annotations to its current holder, but it does not invent roads, treasure, or safe passage where none exists.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 rules
body: Price 1,200 gp; negligible weight; faint divination; caster level 5th; construction requires Craft (mapmaking) 5 ranks, Knowledge (geography) 5 ranks, and access to a divination caster.

After studying the map for 10 minutes, a creature gains a +2 competence bonus on Survival, Knowledge (geography), and Profession (navigator) checks made within the depicted region for the next 24 hours.

Once per day, the holder may spend 10 minutes consulting the map to search for a hidden campsite, cache, landmark, or secondary route within 1 mile. The map reveals one only if such a feature genuinely exists; otherwise it indicates that its memories contain no useful match.
The map becomes unreliable after major island drift, route destruction, planar travel, or deliberate cartographic alteration until updated through fieldwork.

sections.heading: Crafting profile
body: Complexity: Complex; project DC 22; 8 work units; raw materials 400 gp.
Required components: accurate regional survey, durable parchment, inks mixed from at least three landmarks along the route, and a personal travel record from someone who completed the route.
Research skill: Knowledge (geography) or Gather Information. Construction skill: Craft (mapmaking). Testing skill: Profession (navigator) or Survival within the depicted region.
Common flaw: one category of landmark is outdated, or the daily revelation sometimes points toward the map maker’s former preferences rather than the holder’s stated need.

sourceRefs.notes: Converted equipment rules and crafting profile.

entries.title: Etched Skystone
entries.summary: A converted inexpensive navigation and signaling charm that points toward the nearest open sky and emits brief light.
body: An etched skystone is a cool gray fragment carved with winds, constellations, or abstract routes. It hums faintly and turns in the bearer’s palm toward the nearest route to open sky.
Its guidance follows reachable open air rather than the shortest straight line, making it useful in holds, tunnels, ruins, mines, and enclosed fortifications.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 rules
body: Price 150 gp; negligible weight; faint divination and evocation; caster level 1st; construction requires Craft (stonecarving) 3 ranks and either Spellcraft 1 rank or assistance from a minor spellcaster.

When placed on an open palm, the stone points toward the nearest continuous route leading to open sky. It does not identify hazards, locked barriers, distance, or whether the route can be traversed safely.

Striking the stone against a hard surface causes it to shed dim light in a 10-foot radius for 5 rounds. This function can be used at will, but striking it more than once per minute produces no additional effect.
The stone gives no useful direction while already beneath open sky and may become confused inside extradimensional spaces.

sections.heading: Crafting profile
body: Complexity: Standard; project DC 15; 2 work units; raw materials 50 gp.
Required components: naturally buoyant or sky-attuned stone, silver or glow-ink etching material, and exposure to unobstructed sky during final carving.
Research skill: Knowledge (arcana) or Knowledge (geography). Construction skill: Craft (stonecarving). Testing skill: Survival or Search inside a known enclosed route.
Common flaw: the stone points toward the largest opening rather than the nearest, or its light flickers visibly before activation.
